# Rules

<!-- generated by tools/gen_docs.py from unleak/rules.py; do not edit by hand -->

`unleak check` runs the **UL** rules on code; `unleak data` runs the **UD** checks on a real
train/test pair. `unleak explain <RULE>` prints any section below in the terminal.

Severity: **error** = supervised information from evaluation rows reaches training, expect
materially inflated metrics; **warning** = methodologically wrong, effect ranges from tiny to
large; **info** = needs a data check to confirm (hidden unless `--min-severity info`).

| Rule | Severity | Name | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| [UL101](#ul101-preprocessing-before-split) | warning | `preprocessing-before-split` | Preprocessing fitted on rows that end up in the test set |
| [UL102](#ul102-feature-selection-before-split) | error | `feature-selection-before-split` | Supervised feature selection saw the test labels |
| [UL103](#ul103-oversampling-before-split) | error | `oversampling-before-split` | Oversampling ran before the split |
| [UL104](#ul104-undersampling-before-split) | warning | `undersampling-before-split` | Undersampling ran before the split |
| [UL105](#ul105-target-encoding-before-split) | error | `target-encoding-before-split` | Target encoding learned from the test labels |
| [UL106](#ul106-global-statistics-before-split) | warning | `global-statistics-before-split` | Features filled or scaled with statistics of the whole dataset |
| [UL107](#ul107-fit-on-train-and-test) | warning | `fit-on-train-and-test` | Preprocessing fitted on train and test combined |
| [UL201](#ul201-fit-on-test-data) | error | `fit-on-test-data` | A model or transformer was fitted on the test set |
| [UL202](#ul202-model-trained-on-test-rows) | error | `model-trained-on-test-rows` | The model was trained on data that contains the test rows |
| [UL203](#ul203-early-stopping-on-test) | error | `early-stopping-on-test` | Early stopping / best-model selection used the test set |
| [UL204](#ul204-tuning-on-test-set) | warning | `tuning-on-test-set` | Hyperparameters or models were selected by test-set score |
| [UL301](#ul301-target-in-features) | error | `target-in-features` | The target column is still in the feature matrix |
| [UL302](#ul302-feature-built-from-target) | error | `feature-built-from-target` | A feature was computed from the target |
| [UL303](#ul303-target-proxy-in-features) | error | `target-proxy-in-features` | The target was derived from a column that is still a feature |
| [UL401](#ul401-lookahead-feature) | error | `lookahead-feature` | A feature uses values from the future |
| [UL402](#ul402-shuffled-time-series-split) | error | `shuffled-time-series-split` | Time-series features with a random split |
| [UL403](#ul403-ungrouped-entity-split) | info | `ungrouped-entity-split` | Rows belong to entities but the split is not grouped |
| [UD001](#ud001-duplicate-rows-across-splits) | error | `duplicate-rows-across-splits` | Identical rows appear in both train and test |
| [UD002](#ud002-group-overlap) | error | `group-overlap` | The same entity appears in train and test |
| [UD003](#ud003-temporal-overlap) | warning | `temporal-overlap` | Training rows are newer than test rows |
| [UD004](#ud004-near-perfect-feature) | warning | `near-perfect-feature` | A single feature predicts the target almost perfectly |

## UL101 preprocessing-before-split

**Preprocessing fitted on rows that end up in the test set** · severity: `warning`

A scaler, imputer, PCA, vectorizer, clusterer or similar was fitted on data that includes held-out rows. Their statistics (means, variances, vocabulary, components) leak into the training features, so the test score is no longer an estimate of performance on unseen data. The effect is often small for plain scaling and can be large for imputers, PCA, TF-IDF and clustering on small datasets.

**Fix:** Split first, then fit preprocessing on the training rows only. The simplest way is a Pipeline: cross-validation and .fit() then refit the step inside every training fold.

```python
# leaky
X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y)

# fixed
model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression())
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
```

## UL102 feature-selection-before-split

**Supervised feature selection saw the test labels** · severity: `error`

Feature selection that looks at the target (SelectKBest, RFE, SelectFromModel, mutual information, correlation with the target, LDA...) was run on rows that are later used for testing. The selected features are partly chosen *because* they fit the test labels. On high-dimensional data this alone can turn pure noise into an apparently accurate model.

**Fix:** Do selection inside the training data only, e.g. make_pipeline(SelectKBest(k=20), model) evaluated with cross_val_score, or fit the selector on X_train.

```python
# leaky
X_sel = SelectKBest(f_classif, k=20).fit_transform(X, y)
cross_val_score(LogisticRegression(), X_sel, y)

# fixed
pipe = make_pipeline(SelectKBest(f_classif, k=20), LogisticRegression())
cross_val_score(pipe, X, y)
```

## UL103 oversampling-before-split

**Oversampling ran before the split** · severity: `error`

SMOTE, ADASYN and RandomOverSampler create synthetic or duplicated minority rows. Done before splitting, near-copies of the same original rows land on both sides of the split, so the model is tested on rows it has effectively already seen. Minority-class recall and F1 are typically inflated dramatically.

**Fix:** Resample only the training data. With cross-validation, use imblearn.pipeline.make_pipeline(SMOTE(), model) so resampling happens inside each training fold. Never resample the test set.

```python
# leaky
X_res, y_res = SMOTE().fit_resample(X, y)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_res, y_res)

# fixed
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y)
X_train, y_train = SMOTE().fit_resample(X_train, y_train)
```

## UL104 undersampling-before-split

**Undersampling ran before the split** · severity: `warning`

Undersampling before the split changes the class balance of the test set, so test metrics describe an artificial, balanced population instead of the real one. Cleaning methods (Tomek links, ENN) also use the test rows to decide what to drop.

**Fix:** Split first and resample only the training data (or use an imblearn Pipeline). Evaluate on the untouched class distribution.

```python
# leaky
X_res, y_res = RandomUnderSampler().fit_resample(X, y)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_res, y_res)

# fixed
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y)
X_train, y_train = RandomUnderSampler().fit_resample(X_train, y_train)
```

## UL105 target-encoding-before-split

**Target encoding learned from the test labels** · severity: `error`

A target/mean/WOE encoder replaces each category with a statistic of the target. Fitted before the split, test rows' own labels are baked into their encoded features - a direct label leak that is strongest for rare categories.

**Fix:** Fit the encoder on training rows only (inside a Pipeline or the CV loop). sklearn's TargetEncoder cross-fits inside fit_transform, but only when fitted on the training split.

```python
# leaky
X['city'] = TargetEncoder().fit_transform(X[['city']], y)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y)

# fixed
pipe = make_pipeline(TargetEncoder(), HistGradientBoostingClassifier())
pipe.fit(X_train, y_train)
```

## UL106 global-statistics-before-split

**Features filled or scaled with statistics of the whole dataset** · severity: `warning`

A mean, median, std, min/max or quantile computed on all rows was used to impute or normalise features before the train/test split. It is the hand-written version of UL101: test rows influence the values seen during training.

**Fix:** Compute the statistic on the training split and reuse it for the test split, or use SimpleImputer/StandardScaler inside a Pipeline.

```python
# leaky
df['age'] = df['age'].fillna(df['age'].mean())
train, test = train_test_split(df)

# fixed
train, test = train_test_split(df)
mean_age = train['age'].mean()
train['age'] = train['age'].fillna(mean_age)
test['age'] = test['age'].fillna(mean_age)
```

## UL107 fit-on-train-and-test

**Preprocessing fitted on train and test combined** · severity: `warning`

The training and test sets were concatenated and a transformer was fitted on the result. This is common in competitions where test labels are unknown, but any score measured on held-out rows that went into the fit (including a validation split carved from train) is optimistic.

**Fix:** Fit preprocessing on the training rows only, or accept the transductive setup knowingly and do not report its validation score as an unbiased estimate.

```python
# leaky
full = pd.concat([train, test])
scaler.fit(full[cols])

# fixed
scaler.fit(train[cols])
test[cols] = scaler.transform(test[cols])
```

## UL201 fit-on-test-data

**A model or transformer was fitted on the test set** · severity: `error`

Calling fit / fit_transform / fit_resample on test data either trains on the rows you evaluate on, or (for preprocessing) re-learns the transformation from the test data so train and test are encoded inconsistently. Typical bug: X_test = scaler.fit_transform(X_test).

**Fix:** Fit on the training split, then call only transform / predict on the test split.

```python
# leaky
X_train = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test = scaler.fit_transform(X_test)

# fixed
X_train = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test = scaler.transform(X_test)
```

## UL202 model-trained-on-test-rows

**The model was trained on data that contains the test rows** · severity: `error`

The model (or search) was fitted on the full dataset and then evaluated on a subset of that same dataset. Every test row was part of training, so the score measures memorisation, not generalisation.

**Fix:** Fit on X_train only. If you refit on all data for deployment, do it after the evaluation and do not evaluate that refitted model on the old test split.

```python
# leaky
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y)
model.fit(X, y)
model.score(X_test, y_test)

# fixed
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
model.score(X_test, y_test)
```

## UL203 early-stopping-on-test

**Early stopping / best-model selection used the test set** · severity: `error`

The test set was passed as eval_set / validation_data while early stopping or best-iteration selection was active, and the same test set is used to report the final metric. The number of trees or epochs was tuned on the test data, so the reported score is optimistic.

**Fix:** Carve a separate validation split from the training data for early stopping and keep the test set for the final, single evaluation.

```python
# leaky
model.fit(X_train, y_train, eval_set=[(X_test, y_test)],
          early_stopping_rounds=50)
accuracy_score(y_test, model.predict(X_test))

# fixed
X_tr, X_val, y_tr, y_val = train_test_split(X_train, y_train)
model.fit(X_tr, y_tr, eval_set=[(X_val, y_val)])
accuracy_score(y_test, model.predict(X_test))
```

## UL204 tuning-on-test-set

**Hyperparameters or models were selected by test-set score** · severity: `warning`

A loop fits several models or hyperparameter values, scores each on the test set and keeps the best. The winning score is then a maximum over noisy test estimates - it is biased upward, and the test set has become a validation set.

**Fix:** Select with cross-validation (GridSearchCV) or a separate validation split, then evaluate the single chosen model once on the test set.

```python
# leaky
for k in range(1, 30):
    knn = KNeighborsClassifier(k).fit(X_train, y_train)
    acc = knn.score(X_test, y_test)
    if acc > best: best, best_k = acc, k

# fixed
search = GridSearchCV(KNeighborsClassifier(), {'n_neighbors': range(1, 30)})
search.fit(X_train, y_train)
search.score(X_test, y_test)
```

## UL301 target-in-features

**The target column is still in the feature matrix** · severity: `error`

The column used as y was not removed from X, so the model can read the answer directly. Scores near 100% are the usual symptom.

**Fix:** Drop the target (and anything derived from it) when building X, e.g. X = df.drop(columns=[target]).

```python
# leaky
y = df['price']
X = df.drop(columns=['id'])

# fixed
y = df['price']
X = df.drop(columns=['id', 'price'])
```

## UL302 feature-built-from-target

**A feature was computed from the target** · severity: `error`

A feature column was derived from the target column on data that includes held-out rows - for example a groupby mean of the target (hand-rolled target encoding) or a rolling window that includes the current target. The label of each row leaks into its own features.

**Fix:** Compute target-based features on the training split only, using out-of-fold estimates, or shift time-series windows so they only use past targets (.shift(1) before .rolling()).

```python
# leaky
df['city_rate'] = df.groupby('city')['churn'].transform('mean')
X = df.drop(columns=['churn'])

# fixed
rates = train.groupby('city')['churn'].mean()
test['city_rate'] = test['city'].map(rates)
```

## UL303 target-proxy-in-features

**The target was derived from a column that is still a feature** · severity: `error`

The label was computed from another column (a threshold, mapping or formula), and that source column was left in X. The model can reconstruct the label from it without learning anything useful.

**Fix:** Drop the column(s) the target was derived from, or redefine the task so the features are only things known before the outcome.

```python
# leaky
df['high_value'] = (df['revenue'] > 1000).astype(int)
X = df.drop(columns=['high_value'])

# fixed
df['high_value'] = (df['revenue'] > 1000).astype(int)
X = df.drop(columns=['high_value', 'revenue'])
```

## UL401 lookahead-feature

**A feature uses values from the future** · severity: `error`

A feature was built with a negative shift or a centred rolling window, so each row can see values recorded after it. Fine for constructing the *target*, never for a feature. (If your data is sorted newest-first, a negative shift points to the past; add an ignore comment in that case.)

**Fix:** Use positive shifts for lag features and center=False (the default) for rolling windows.

```python
# leaky
df['next_close'] = df['close'].shift(-1)
df['trend'] = df['close'].rolling(7, center=True).mean()

# fixed
df['prev_close'] = df['close'].shift(1)
df['trend'] = df['close'].rolling(7).mean().shift(1)
```

## UL402 shuffled-time-series-split

**Time-series features with a random split** · severity: `error`

The data has lag/rolling/diff features, but rows were split randomly (train_test_split shuffles by default; ShuffleSplit and KFold(shuffle=True) too). Training rows then come from after the test rows, and overlapping windows copy test information into training features.

**Fix:** Split by time: train_test_split(..., shuffle=False) on data sorted by time, TimeSeriesSplit for cross-validation, or a date cutoff.

```python
# leaky
df['lag_1'] = df['sales'].shift(1)
train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2)

# fixed
df = df.sort_values('date')
train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, shuffle=False)
cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=TimeSeriesSplit(5))
```

## UL403 ungrouped-entity-split

**Rows belong to entities but the split is not grouped** · severity: `info`

The data has an entity identifier (patient_id, user_id...) but the split is row-wise. If an entity has several rows, the same patient or user ends up in both train and test and the model is rewarded for recognising them. Verify with `unleak data --group <col>`.

**Fix:** Split with GroupShuffleSplit / GroupKFold / StratifiedGroupKFold using the entity id as groups.

```python
# leaky
train_test_split(X, y)  # df has several rows per patient_id

# fixed
GroupShuffleSplit(test_size=0.2).split(X, y, groups=df['patient_id'])
```

## UD001 duplicate-rows-across-splits

**Identical rows appear in both train and test** · severity: `error`

Rows with identical feature values are present on both sides of the split. The model is tested on examples it was trained on - common after oversampling, augmentation or merging data sources.

**Fix:** Deduplicate before splitting, or split by a key that keeps duplicates together.

```python
# leaky
df = pd.concat([df, df_augmented]); train_test_split(df)

# fixed
df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=feature_cols); train_test_split(df)
```

## UD002 group-overlap

**The same entity appears in train and test** · severity: `error`

Values of the group column (e.g. patient_id) occur in both splits, so the test set is not made of new entities.

**Fix:** Use GroupShuffleSplit / GroupKFold with this column as groups.

```python
# leaky
train_test_split(df)

# fixed
GroupShuffleSplit().split(df, groups=df['patient_id'])
```

## UD003 temporal-overlap

**Training rows are newer than test rows** · severity: `warning`

Some training rows have timestamps later than the earliest test row. For forecasting-type problems this means the model learns from the future of the period it is evaluated on.

**Fix:** Use a time cutoff: train on rows before date T, test on rows after.

```python
# leaky
train_test_split(df)

# fixed
train, test = df[df.date < cutoff], df[df.date >= cutoff]
```

## UD004 near-perfect-feature

**A single feature predicts the target almost perfectly** · severity: `warning`

One column alone separates the classes (AUC >= 0.99) or tracks the target (|correlation| >= 0.99). Real-world signal is rarely that clean; this is the classic signature of target leakage through a proxy column (an outcome recorded after the fact, an id assigned by label, a duplicated target).

**Fix:** Check how the column is produced and whether it is available at prediction time. Drop it if not.

```python
# leaky
X = df.drop(columns=['default'])  # still has 'days_in_collections'

# fixed
X = df.drop(columns=['default', 'days_in_collections'])
```

Suppress a deliberate case with `# unleak: ignore[RULE]` on the reported line, or a whole file with `# unleak: skip-file`.
